    example: 'np 60 dół 45 np 60',
    mode: '3d',
  },
  {
    id: 'pp',
    title: 'Przechyl w prawo',
    polish: ['pp', 'przechylprawo'],
    english: ['rr', 'rollright'],
    argument: 'wyrażenie (kąt w stopniach)',
    meaning: 'Tylko 3D. Przechyla żółwia w prawo wokół kierunku ruchu: jego góra obraca się w stronę jego prawej strony. Kierunek się nie zmienia.',
    example: 'pp 90 pw 90 np 60',
    mode: '3d',
  },
  {
    id: 'pl',
    title: 'Przechyl w lewo',
    polish: ['pl', 'przechyllewo'],
    english: ['rl', 'rollleft'],
    argument: 'wyrażenie (kąt w stopniach)',
    meaning: 'Tylko 3D. Przechyla żółwia w lewo wokół kierunku ruchu.',
    example: 'pl 90 pw 90 np 60',
    mode: '3d',
  },
];

export interface Topic {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  /** Paragraphs; a string starting with "```" is a runnable example: "```2d\ncode". */
  body: (string | { code: string; mode: Mode; note?: string } | { list: string[] } | { table: string[][] })[];
}

  {

# Logomocja

A Polish-language web studio for turtle drawing, inspired by the classic Polish Logo environment of the same name. You write a Logo program, run it or step through it, and watch the turtle draw on a plane (2D) or in space (3D). The interface is in Polish. There are no accounts, no backend and no network access at runtime.

## What's inside

- **Pracownia** (workspace): an editor with line numbers, syntax highlighting, an inline error marker (line, column and a Polish message) and a highlight on the line being executed. Controls: run, step, pause/resume, reset, a speed slider and an operations meter. The 2D view supports pan, zoom, fit and shows the origin. The 3D view (three.js) supports orbit, pan, zoom, camera reset, a ground grid and axes. Files: open/save `.logo`, a permalink, PNG export.
- **Przykłady**: the 13 standard programs, verbatim, each loaded into its own mode. An unsaved draft that would be replaced is kept and can be restored with "Przywróć szkic".
- **Zadania**: 8 challenges checked automatically against the expected drawing. Lines may be split, reordered or reversed, and the drawing may be moved as a whole; the tolerance is 2 units. Progress is kept in `localStorage`.
- **Pomoc**: a reference for the whole dialect, with a "Wypróbuj" (try it) button on every example.

Keyboard shortcuts: `Ctrl/⌘+Enter` runs (or resumes), `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` steps, `Esc` pauses or resumes, `Ctrl+Shift+Backspace` resets. The list is shown under the editor and in Pomoc.

## Running

Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh).

```sh
bun install
bun run dev        # development server
bun run build      # static site in dist/
bun run preview    # serve dist/ locally
bun run test       # interpreter and app tests (Vitest + jsdom)
```

### Building for a sub-path

The build honours `BASE_PATH` (default `/`):

```sh
BASE_PATH=/Logomocja/builds/x/ bun run build
```

`dist/` is a set of plain static files. Routes use the URL hash (`#/przyklady`, `#/zadania`, `#/pomoc/procedury`, …), so a refresh on any route works on a static host with no rewrite rules. Fonts (Lexend, JetBrains Mono) and every library are bundled locally.

## Testing hook

Once the page has loaded, `window.logomocja` provides:

- `version`: a string.
- `run(source, mode)`: interprets the program without touching the UI and returns `{ segments, error }`.
- `open(source, mode)`: loads the program into the editor, runs it without animation, fits the view and returns a Promise of `{ segments, error }` once the drawing is on screen.

`mode` is `"2d"` or `"3d"`. A segment is `{ from: [x,y,z], to: [x,y,z], color: "#rrggbb", width }`. An error is `null` or `{ message, line, column }`.

## Project layout

```
src/lang/        interpreter: lexer, parser (whole-program validation), executor (generator, one operation per step)
src/content/     standard programs, challenges with the checker, the reference content
src/app/         UI: shell and routing (app.ts), workspace, editor, 2D and 3D views, execution controller, storage, permalinks
tests/           Vitest: interpreter, examples, challenges, controller, app flows (jsdom), testing hook
```

## Tests and what they cover

- `tests/interpreter.test.ts`, `tests/examples.test.ts`: the `run(source, mode)` interface. Covers strokes in 2D and 3D, expressions and the operator-spacing rule, errors and their positions, limits, scoping, `stop`, `nrpowt`, and the 13 standard programs.
- `tests/controller.test.ts`: the execution controller used by the buttons (run, step, pause, resume, reset), with time driven by a manual scheduler.
- `tests/app.test.ts`, `tests/hook.test.ts`: the app mounted in jsdom and driven through its buttons. Covers `open()`, controls and shortcuts, the error marker, editing during a run, per-mode drafts, examples and draft preservation, permalinks, `.logo` files, challenges and persisted progress, and the reference content.

Not covered by tests: canvas and WebGL pixel output, real-browser layout and visual quality. jsdom has no canvas or WebGL; in that environment the 3D view reports that it is off, which exercises the no-WebGL path.

## Design

Design context lives in `PRODUCT.md`, `DESIGN.md` and `.impeccable/`. None of these files ship to `dist/`.

# Logomocja

A Polish-language web studio for turtle drawing, inspired by the classic Polish Logo environment of the same name. You write a Logo program, run it or step through it, and watch the turtle draw on a plane (2D) or in space (3D). The interface is in Polish. There are no accounts, no backend and no network access at runtime.

## What's inside

- **Pracownia** (workspace): an editor with line numbers, syntax highlighting, an inline error marker (line, column and a Polish message) and a highlight on the line being executed. Controls: run, step, pause/resume, reset, a speed slider and an operations meter. The 2D view supports pan, zoom, fit and shows the origin. The 3D view (three.js) supports orbit, pan, zoom, camera reset, a ground grid and axes. Files: open/save `.logo`, a permalink, PNG export.
- **Przykłady**: the 13 standard programs, verbatim, each loaded into its own mode. An unsaved draft that would be replaced is kept and can be restored with "Przywróć szkic".
- **Zadania**: 8 challenges checked automatically against the expected drawing. Lines may be split, reordered or reversed, and the drawing may be moved as a whole; the tolerance is 2 units. Progress is kept in `localStorage`.
- **Pomoc**: a reference for the whole dialect, with a "Wypróbuj" (try it) button on every example.

Keyboard shortcuts: `Ctrl/⌘+Enter` runs (or resumes), `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` steps, `Esc` pauses or resumes, `Ctrl+Shift+Backspace` resets. The list is shown under the editor and in Pomoc.

## Running

Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh).

```sh
bun install
bun run dev        # development server
bun run build      # static site in dist/
bun run preview    # serve dist/ locally
bun run test       # interpreter and app tests (Vitest + jsdom)
```

### Building for a sub-path

The build honours `BASE_PATH` (default `/`):

```sh
BASE_PATH=/Logomocja/builds/x/ bun run build
```

`dist/` is a set of plain static files. Routes use the URL hash (`#/przyklady`, `#/zadania`, `#/pomoc/procedury`, …), so a refresh on any route works on a static host with no rewrite rules. Fonts (Lexend, JetBrains Mono) and every library are bundled locally.

## Testing hook

Once the page has loaded, `window.logomocja` provides:

- `version`: a string.
- `run(source, mode)`: interprets the program without touching the UI and returns `{ segments, error }`.
- `open(source, mode)`: loads the program into the editor, runs it without animation, fits the view and returns a Promise of `{ segments, error }` once the drawing is on screen.

`mode` is `"2d"` or `"3d"`. A segment is `{ from: [x,y,z], to: [x,y,z], color: "#rrggbb", width }`. An error is `null` or `{ message, line, column }`.

## Project layout

```
src/lang/        interpreter: lexer, parser (whole-program validation), executor (generator, one operation per step)
src/content/     standard programs, challenges with the checker, the reference content
src/app/         UI: shell and routing (app.ts), workspace, editor, 2D and 3D views, execution controller, storage, permalinks
tests/           Vitest: interpreter, examples, challenges, controller, app flows (jsdom), testing hook
```

## Tests and what they cover

- `tests/interpreter.test.ts`, `tests/examples.test.ts`: the `run(source, mode)` interface. Covers strokes in 2D and 3D, expressions and the operator-spacing rule, errors and their positions, limits, scoping, `stop`, `nrpowt`, and the 13 standard programs.
- `tests/controller.test.ts`: the execution controller used by the buttons (run, step, pause, resume, reset), with time driven by a manual scheduler.
- `tests/app.test.ts`, `tests/hook.test.ts`: the app mounted in jsdom and driven through its buttons. Covers `open()`, controls and shortcuts, the error marker, editing during a run, per-mode drafts, examples and draft preservation, permalinks, `.logo` files, challenges and persisted progress, and the reference content.

Not covered by tests: canvas and WebGL pixel output, real-browser layout and visual quality. jsdom has no canvas or WebGL; in that environment the 3D view reports that it is off, which exercises the no-WebGL path.

## Design

Design context lives in `PRODUCT.md`, `DESIGN.md` and `.impeccable/`. None of these files ship to `dist/`.

Generate a `DESIGN.md` file at the project root that captures the current visual design system, so AI agents generating new screens stay on-brand.

DESIGN.md follows the [official DESIGN.md format spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-labs-code/design.md/main/docs/spec.md): optional YAML frontmatter carrying machine-readable design tokens, followed by up to eight markdown sections in a fixed order. **Tokens are normative; prose provides context for how to apply them.** Sections may be omitted when not relevant, but those present stay in the specified order. Use the canonical headings below so the file remains portable across DESIGN.md-aware tools.

## The frontmatter: token schema

The YAML frontmatter is the machine-readable layer. It's what Stitch's linter validates and what the live panel renders tiles from. Keep it tight; every entry should correspond to a token the project actually uses.

```yaml
---
name: <project title>
description: <one-line tagline>
colors:
  primary: "#b8422e"
  neutral-bg: "#faf7f2"
  # ...one entry per extracted color; key = descriptive slug
typography:
  display:
    fontFamily: "Cormorant Garamond, Georgia, serif"
    fontSize: "clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 4.5rem)"
    fontWeight: 300
    lineHeight: 1
    letterSpacing: "normal"
  body:
    # ...
rounded:
  sm: "4px"
  md: "8px"
spacing:
  sm: "8px"
  md: "16px"
components:
  button-primary:
    backgroundColor: "{colors.primary}"
    textColor: "{colors.neutral-bg}"
    rounded: "{rounded.sm}"
    padding: "16px 48px"
  button-primary-hover:
    backgroundColor: "{colors.primary-deep}"
---
```

Rules that matter:

- **Token refs** use `{path.to.token}` (e.g. `{colors.primary}`, `{rounded.md}`). Components may reference primitives; primitives may not reference each other.
- **Colors accept any valid CSS color string.** Hex is the recommended default for portability, but preserve an incumbent `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `oklch()`, wide-gamut, or mixed-color value when it is the project's normative source. Never split the source of truth without explicit reason.
- **Component sub-tokens** are limited to 8 props: `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `typography`, `rounded`, `padding`, `size`, `height`, `width`. Shadows, motion, focus rings, backdrop-filter: none of those fit. Carry them in the sidecar (Step 4b).
- **Scale keys are open-ended.** Use whatever names the project already uses (`oxblood-deep`, `surface-container-low`). Don't rename to Material defaults.
- **Variants are naming convention, not schema.** `button-primary` / `button-primary-hover` / `button-primary-active` as sibling keys.

## The markdown body: eight sections (canonical order)

1. `## Overview`
2. `## Colors`
3. `## Typography`
4. `## Layout`
5. `## Elevation & Depth`
6. `## Shapes`
7. `## Components`
8. `## Do's and Don'ts`

Omit irrelevant sections rather than filling them with invented rules. Put responsive layout in Layout, depth in Elevation & Depth, radius and form language in Shapes, and per-component behavior in Components. Unknown sections are preserved by the format, but new visual guidance should use the canonical structure whenever it fits.

## When to run

- New-work found a coherent incumbent visual system but no `DESIGN.md`.
- The first implementation of a new world is complete and its provisional decisions need to be carbonized.
- An existing `DESIGN.md` is stale (the design has drifted).
- Before a large redesign, to capture the current state as a reference.

If a `DESIGN.md` already exists, **do not silently overwrite it**. Show the user the existing file first. Ask with Codex's structured user-input/question tool when available, or directly in chat if it is not, and wait for the answer before continuing. The choice is refresh, overwrite, or merge.

## Two paths

- **Scan mode** (default): the project has design tokens, components, or rendered output. Extract, then confirm descriptive language. Use when there's code to analyze.
- **Seed mode**: the project is pre-implementation. Ensure PRODUCT.md exists, then reuse new-work's visual-world workshop and write its directional DESIGN.md seed. Re-run in scan mode once there's code.

Decide by scanning first (Scan mode Step 1). If the scan finds no tokens, no component files, and no rendered site, offer seed mode; don't silently switch. `$impeccable document --seed` requests new-work's world workshop, but it does not authorize replacing coherent code: when an incumbent system exists, offer scan mode or route an explicit identity-replacement request through new-work.

## Scan mode (approach C: auto-extract, then confirm descriptive language)

### Step 1: Find the design assets

Search the codebase in priority order:

1. **CSS custom properties**: grep for `--color-`, `--font-`, `--spacing-`, `--radius-`, `--shadow-`, `--ease-`, `--duration-` declarations in CSS files (usually `src/styles/`, `public/css/`, `app/globals.css`, etc.). Record name, value, and the file it's defined in.
2. **Tailwind config**: if `tailwind.config.{js,ts,mjs}` exists, read the `theme.extend` block for colors, fontFamily, spacing, borderRadius, boxShadow.
3. **CSS-in-JS theme files**: styled-components, emotion, vanilla-extract, stitches; look for `theme.ts`, `tokens.ts`, or equivalent.
4. **Design token files**: `tokens.json`, `design-tokens.json`, Style Dictionary output, W3C token community group format.
5. **Component library**: scan the main button, card, input, navigation, dialog components. Note their variant APIs and default styles.
6. **Global stylesheet**: the root CSS file usually has the base typography and color assignments.
7. **Visible rendered output**: if browser automation tools are available, load the live site and sample computed styles from key elements (body, h1, a, button, .card). This catches values that tokens miss.

### Step 2: Auto-extract what can be auto-extracted

Build a structured draft from the discovered tokens. For each token class:

- **Colors**: Group into Primary / Secondary / Tertiary / Neutral (the Material-derived roles Stitch uses). If the project only has one accent, express it as Primary + Neutral; omit Secondary and Tertiary rather than inventing them.
- **Typography**: Map observed sizes and weights to the Material hierarchy (display / headline / title / body / label). Note font-family stacks and the scale ratio.
- **Elevation**: Catalogue the shadow vocabulary. If the project is flat and uses tonal layering instead, that's a valid answer; state it explicitly.
- **Components**: For each common component (button, card, input, chip, list item, tooltip, nav), extract shape (radius), color assignment, hover/focus treatment, internal padding.
- **Layout + spacing**: Extract grid, container, breakpoint, rhythm, and density behavior into Layout.
- **Shapes**: Extract radius, corner, border, clipping, and recurring form behavior into Shapes.

### Step 2b: Stage the frontmatter

From the auto-extracted tokens, draft the YAML frontmatter now (you'll write it at the top of DESIGN.md in Step 4). This is the machine-readable layer: what the live panel and Stitch's linter consume.

- **Colors**: one entry per extracted color. Key = descriptive slug (`oxblood-deep`, `editorial-magenta`, not `blue-800`). Value = whichever format the project treats as canonical (OKLCH or hex; see the frontmatter rules above). Don't split the source of truth: one format in the frontmatter, don't redefine the same token in prose with a different value.
- **Typography**: one entry per role (`display`, `headline`, `title`, `body`, `label`). Typography is an object; include only the props that are real for the project (`fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `fontFeature`, `fontVariation`).
- **Rounded / Spacing**: whatever scale steps the project actually uses, keyed by whatever scale name the project uses (`sm` / `md` / `lg`, or `surface-sm`, or numeric steps).
- **Components**: one entry per variant (`button-primary`, `button-primary-hover`, `button-ghost`). Reference primitives via `{colors.X}`, `{rounded.Y}`. If a variant needs a property Stitch's 8-prop set doesn't cover (shadow, focus ring, backdrop-filter), carry the full snippet in the sidecar instead.

Skip anything the project doesn't have. Empty scale keys or fabricated tokens pollute the spec.

### Step 3: Ask the user for qualitative language

The following require creative input that cannot be auto-extracted. Ask them in two structured rounds of no more than three questions each (or the harness's lower limit), waiting between rounds:

- **Creative North Star**: a single named metaphor for the whole system ("The Editorial Sanctuary", "The Golden State Curator", "The Lab Notebook"). Offer 2-3 options that honor PRODUCT.md's brand personality.
- **Overview voice**: mood adjectives, aesthetic philosophy in 2-3 sentences, and any confirmed visual anti-reference.
- **Color character** (for auto-extracted colors): descriptive names ("Deep Muted Teal-Navy", not "blue-800"). Suggest 2-3 options per key color based on hue/saturation.
- **Elevation philosophy**: flat/layered/lifted. If shadows exist, is their role ambient or structural?
- **Component philosophy**: the feel of buttons, cards, inputs in one phrase ("tactile and confident" vs. "refined and restrained").

Carry a line from PRODUCT.md only when it is a durable brand commitment that actually constrains the visual system. Page strategy and surface concepts do not belong here.

### Step 4: Write DESIGN.md

The file opens with the YAML frontmatter staged in Step 2b (schema documented at the top of this reference), then the markdown body using the canonical structure below.

```markdown
---
name: [Project Title]
description: [one-line tagline]
colors:
  # ... staged frontmatter from Step 2b
---

# Design System: [Project Title]

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "[Named metaphor in quotes]"**

[2-3 paragraph holistic description: personality, density, and aesthetic philosophy. Start from the North Star and work outward. State only confirmed visual rejections. End with a short **Key Characteristics:** bullet list.]

## Colors

[Describe the palette character in one sentence.]

# Design System: Logomocja

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "The Łowicz Cut-Out"**

Logomocja looks like a wycinanka, the layered paper cut-out from Łowicz: flat, saturated pieces of coloured paper laid on a plain sheet. The sheet is white in the light theme and black in the dark one, as cut-outs are glued to either. Colour is never decoration. Each of the four sections owns one paper colour, and that colour runs under the whole top bar as a 4px band while you are in the section. The drawing is the reward, so the canvas is the largest calm surface on the screen.

It is a working tool (Operate mode). The layout, navigation and controls are the familiar ones for a code playground: tabs, a toolbar, an editor next to a canvas, and plain buttons and sliders. The world shows up only in palette, type, density and one signature element, the progress rosette.

**Key Characteristics:**
- White or black sheet, never grey; neutrals are slightly green-tinted.
- One saturated hue per section: green Pracownia, marigold Przykłady, fuchsia Zadania, cobalt Pomoc.
- Flat layers: depth comes from coloured bands under elements, not from shadows.
- Vermilion appears only for errors.
- The rosette: one cut-paper petal per challenge, coloured in when solved.

## Colors

A cut-out palette of four saturated papers, plus violet for 3D, on a neutral sheet. In dark mode every hue is lifted so it keeps its contrast on black.

### Primary
- **Meadow Green** (#187a35; dark #3fbf68): the Pracownia hue. The Run button, the active Pracownia tab and band, the operations meter fill, the speed slider accent, the Y axis.

### Secondary
- **Marigold** (#f2a516; dark #f5b335): the Przykłady hue. Also marks the executing line (a gutter block plus a pale line band, #fdf1d6) and the draft-restore notice. Text on it is always ink.
- **Łowicz Fuchsia** (#c8186e; dark #f0559c): the Zadania hue. The Check button, the challenge banner band (#fbe4ef), solved status, target ghost strokes and the X axis.
- **Cobalt** (#2346a8; dark #7f9cf5): the Pomoc hue. Command words in code, reference heading underlines, links, the focus ring and the Z axis.

### Tertiary
- **Plum Violet** (#6b3fa0): 3D-only chips and the 3D example card band; variable names in code.

### Neutral
- **Sheet** (#ffffff / #141614): panels and cards.
- **Ground** (#f2f4ef / #0b0c0b): the page behind the panels.
- **Ink** (#161a17 / #f1f3ed), **Ink 2** (#4a524c / #b2b9b0), **Ink 3** (#616a62 / #8c948a): text in three strengths. All reach at least 5:1 on sheet and ground.
- **Line** (#d7dcd3) and **Line Strong** (#b9c0b6): hairlines and unsolved rosette petals.

### Named Rules
**The One Paper Per Room Rule.** Each section owns exactly one hue. The current section's hue fills the active tab and the band under the top bar; other hues appear there only as content.

**The Vermilion Is Errors Rule.** Error Vermilion (#c63218, text #ad2c13) marks errors only: the inline error flag, the wavy underline, the error gutter cell and the status text. Destructive actions use ink, not vermilion.

## Typography

**UI Font:** Lexend (self-hosted; fallback system-ui)
**Code Font:** JetBrains Mono (self-hosted; fallback ui-monospace)

**Character:** Lexend is a wide, open sans designed for reading fluency, which suits learners. JetBrains Mono is used only for code, coordinates and URLs, never for decoration.

### Hierarchy
- **Headline** (600, 28px, 1.2, -0.02em): page titles (Przykłady, Zadania, Pomoc); 24px on phones.
- **Section** (600, 22px, -0.015em): reference section headings, underlined by a 3px cobalt band.
- **Title** (600, 17px, -0.01em): card name plates and command names.
- **Body** (400, 15px, 1.5): running text; reference prose is capped at 74ch.
- **Label** (500, 13–14px): buttons, tabs, status text.
- **Code** (400, 14px/22px; 15px/23px on phones): the editor and code blocks (13px/20px), with ligatures off.

**The Fixed Scale Rule.** Sizes are fixed px steps (11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 22, 28), not fluid type.

## Layout

The workspace is a two-column grid: editor column `minmax(360px, 42%)`, canvas `1fr`, a 12px gap and 12px padding, filling the viewport under a 56px top bar. At 820px and below the sections move to a fixed bottom bar of four 58px tabs, the canvas moves above the editor (44vh, minimum 260px), and toolbar targets grow to 44px. Content pages are centred at a maximum of 1160px with a card grid of `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(250px, 1fr))` and a 16px gap. The reference adds a 220px sticky table of contents. Spacing runs on a 4/8/12/16/24px rhythm.

## Elevation & Depth

The system is flat; there are no shadows. Depth comes from paper layering: a 3–4px band of colour under an element (the top bar, card art, the challenge banner, reference headings) shows a layer beneath it. Panels are separated from the ground by a 1px line and the sheet colour.

**The Under-Layer Rule.** To lift something, put a coloured band under it. Never add a blur shadow.

## Shapes

Gently rounded rectangles: 12px for panels and cards, 8px for buttons, tabs and notices, 4px for flags, keys and inline code, and pills for chips only. The one organic shape is the petal, used in the rosette, the wordmark star and the favicon, with a punched circular notch.

## Components

### Buttons
- **Shape:** 8px radius; 38px tall (32px small, 44px in the phone toolbar).
- **Primary:** Meadow Green with white text (Uruchom, "Wczytaj i uruchom"); on Przykłady it switches to Marigold with ink text.
- **Challenge:** Łowicz Fuchsia with white text (Sprawdź, Rozwiąż).
- **Secondary:** sheet with a Line Strong border. **Quiet:** transparent, ink-2 text, tinted on hover.
- **Hover / Focus:** 150ms colour transitions, a 1px press on :active, and a 3px cobalt focus ring offset by 2px. Disabled buttons sit at 45% opacity.
- **Destructive:** ink outline that fills with ink when armed, and needs a second click (Wyzeruj postęp). Destructive actions sit apart from their neighbours.

### Navigation
- Tabs hang from the bottom of the top bar. The active tab is filled with its section hue and joins the 4px band below; inactive tabs are ink-2 and tinted on hover. On phones they become a bottom bar with the icon above the label.

### Segmented switch (2D / 3D)
- A tinted track with two 32px buttons; the pressed one is filled with ink. Uses `aria-pressed`.

### Editor
- A gutter with tabular line numbers, then a transparent textarea over a highlighted layer. Code colours: commands in cobalt, numbers in amber-brown, names in violet, colour strings in fuchsia with a 3px underline swatch of their own colour, comments in ink-3 italic, brackets and `oto/już` in green. The executing line gets a marigold gutter block and a pale band. An error gets a vermilion gutter cell, a wavy underline on the token and an error flag (error-lens style) after the end of the line.

### Cards
- Example cards and challenge cards: a live thumbnail on the paper, a 3px band under it (marigold for 2D examples, violet for 3D, fuchsia for solved challenges), a name plate (title and mode chip), one line of text and the action.

### Progress rosette (signature)
- One petal per challenge, arranged radially. Unsolved petals are outlines in Line Strong; solved petals are filled with the section wheel (green, marigold, fuchsia, cobalt), and their notch is punched through to the sheet. 30px in the top bar, 112px on Zadania.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do:
- **Do** give every new section or area exactly one hue from the wheel, and run it under the top bar.
- **Do** keep the sheet pure white (#ffffff) or near-black (#141614).
- **Do** show depth with a 3–4px coloured under-layer band.
- **Do** keep code, coordinates and URLs in JetBrains Mono and everything else in Lexend.
- **Do** keep text at 4.5:1 or better on its ground in both themes.

### Don't:
- **Don't** use vermilion for anything but errors, including destructive buttons.
- **Don't** add blur or offset shadows, glass or gradients.
- **Don't** put a coloured stripe on the side of a line, card or callout; mark the gutter instead.
- **Don't** set small tracked uppercase labels above headings.
- **Don't** use a grey sheet or a warm cream ground.

# Design System: Logomocja

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "The Łowicz Cut-Out"**

Logomocja looks like a wycinanka, the layered paper cut-out from Łowicz: flat, saturated pieces of coloured paper laid on a plain sheet. The sheet is white in the light theme and black in the dark one, as cut-outs are glued to either. Colour is never decoration. Each of the four sections owns one paper colour, and that colour runs under the whole top bar as a 4px band while you are in the section. - The rosette: one cut-paper petal per challenge, coloured in when solved.

content.text:
Logomocja is built in `/work`, but I never saw it rendered: the container has no browser and I wasn't allowed to install one. Everything below is verified by tests or by serving the built files; nothing about how it looks is.

**Verified:**
- `bun install`, `bun run build` and `bun run test` all succeed: 165 tests pass.
- I built with `BASE_PATH=/Logomocja/builds/x/` and served `dist/` from that sub-path on a plain static server. All 18 linked assets returned 200. Routes use the URL hash, so a refresh works without rewrite rules.
- `window.logomocja` has a test of its own: `version`, `run(source, mode)` and `open(source, mode)` return `{ segments, error }` as the brief specifies.

**What's in the app:** all eleven required features. The parts that involve choices of mine:
- **Examples:** the 13 standard programs ship verbatim. Loading one over an unsaved draft keeps the draft, with a "Przywróć szkic" (restore draft) button. Opening a link or a `.logo` file works the same way.
- **Challenges:** there are 8. Your drawing is compared with a reference solution within 2 units. Splitting, reordering or reversing lines is fine, and so is moving the whole drawing.
- **Shortcuts:** Ctrl/⌘+Enter runs or resumes, Ctrl+Shift+Enter steps, Esc pauses or resumes, Ctrl+Shift+Backspace resets. They're listed under the editor and in the reference page.

**Interpreter details:**
- **3D bug, fixed:** mixing pitch and roll made the turtle's orientation shrink, and the 3D tree example lost strokes. The orientation is now re-normalized after every turn.
- **Snapped values:** turns that are multiples of 30° use exact sine and cosine values, and output coordinates are rounded to 1e-9.
- **Unclear rules:** where the brief was ambiguous I picked one reading. An iteration cut short by `stop` doesn't count as a finishing operation, but the procedure call ending does. When a program has several errors, the first `oto`/`już` structure problem is reported before others.

**How the tests map to the agreed seams:**
- **Interpreter** (`run`): strokes in 2D and 3D, every error position and message, limits, scoping, `stop`, `nrpowt`, and all 13 standard programs. Expected values come from the brief or from counting by hand.
- **Execution controls:** the controller behind the buttons, with time faked: run, step, pause, resume, reset.
- **Editor integration and product flows:** the app mounted in jsdom and driven through its buttons. This covers `open()`, controls and shortcuts, the inline error marker, editing during a run, per-mode drafts, example and draft preservation, links, `.logo` files, challenges with saved progress, and the reference covering every alias.
- **Not covered:** jsdom has no canvas or WebGL, so no actual drawing, 3D rendering, PNG export or layout was ever checked. The "3D is off" message path is the only 3D path that ran.

**Design process:**
- I made every product and design decision myself from the brief, as the benchmark allowed; the inferred points are labelled in `PRODUCT.md`.
- The randomized concept roll assigned a Łowicz paper cut-out look. Each section has its own colour, red is used only for errors, and a progress rosette with one petal per challenge fills in as you solve them. The full brief is in `.impeccable/surfaces/index-html.md`.
- The automated design check found nothing. Colour contrast passes the WCAG AA accessibility standard in both themes; I checked it by calculation, not by eye.
- The final design review had to run in this same session (no separate reviewers available). It returned **recapture**: it needs desktop and phone screenshots I can't take here, so there is no pass verdict. The record is `.impeccable/review/finish-review.md`.
- I wrote `DESIGN.md` and `.impeccable/design.json` from the built code.

**Still to do:** capture desktop (1440 wide) and phone (390 wide) screenshots in a real browser and run the design review on them. That's also the first chance to see the 3D view and the canvas output at all.

`README.md` covers running, building, testing and the project layout.
